- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid overcorrecting downward; add 2–5% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges mean reversion — align forecast with 10–15 day moving average of history.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is volatile, forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.  
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome by >3% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is positive but price drops sharply, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 1–2 day lagged sentiment to adjust downward bias.
